title: Deep learning detects and classifies airway nodules on low-dose CT
summary: A center-point matching detection network, adapted from lung nodule detection, reached 73.7% sensitivity on an independent test of 738 proximal airway nodules across four hospitals. In a human-AI interaction test, radiologist sensitivity rose from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1 from 49.4% to 77.2% with AI assistance. A separate 3D SEResNeXt101 model classified 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) and was evaluated on an independent set; the study is retrospective and the classification set is small.
ai_technology: Center-points matching detection network (transfer from lung nodules, with coordinate and multiscale attention) and a 3D SEResNeXt101 classifier on low-dose CT
organization: Nanhua Hospital, University of South China; Xiangya Hospital, Central South University

evidence.tested: Independent multi-hospital test set (738 proximal nodules) plus a human-AI reader comparison; retrospective data.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, effect on interval or post-screen cancer outcomes and generalization of the classifier; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Detects overlooked airway nodules and classifies benign versus malignant ones as a second-reading tool.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
